Load packages.
```{r load packages, echo = FALSE}

library(Seurat)
library(tidyverse)
library(RCurl)
library(cowplot)
library(patchwork)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(colorspace)
library(SCpubr)
library(SeuratWrappers)
library(presto)
library(ggrepel)
library(simspec)


source("/home/marinani/Scripts/Data_analysis/feature_plots.r")

```

```{r load objects}

# load the objects
hto1 <- Read10X("/links/groups/treutlein/DATA/sequencing/20220825_P2092_MARINA_Mg_opt_and_BVO_HTO_repeat/processed/HTO_Mg_rep1/umi_count/", gene.column = 1) %>%  # input = sparse matrix (rows = tags, columns = cells)
        as.matrix %>%                                                                                                                                             # conversion of the S4 object sparse matrix into a normal R matrix
        t %>%                                                                                                                                                     # transpose the matrix
        `colnames<-`(., str_extract(colnames(.), "HTO[0-9]+|unmapped"))                                                                                           # this last line is a tidyverse based way to change the names of the columns. The syntax sets as "colnames" any component of a column name that has the word "HTO" + a number or "unmapped". 

hto2 <- Read10X("/links/groups/treutlein/DATA/sequencing/20220825_P2092_MARINA_Mg_opt_and_BVO_HTO_repeat/processed/HTO_Mg_rep2/umi_count/", gene.column = 1) %>%  
        as.matrix %>%                                                                                                                                            
        t %>%                                                                                                                                                    
        `colnames<-`(., str_extract(colnames(.), "HTO[0-9]+|unmapped"))     

# Delete the column 14, which corresponds to unmapped reads and confounds downstream processing
hto1 <- hto1[,c(-11, -13, -14)]
hto2 <- hto2[,c(-11, -13, -14)]

# Have a look at the objects
head(hto1, n=50)
head(hto2, n=50)

```

```{r wrangle and transpose the matrices}

# Save the hashtag count matrix (hashtags in rownames) to use with HTODemux
hto1 <- t(hto1)
hto2 <- t(hto2)

# Have a look at the matrices
rownames(hto1)
rownames(hto2)

```

```{r save the matrices}

setwd( "Objects/Protocol_optimization/")

# Save the hashtag matrix to bind it to the Seurat object as HTO assay
saveRDS(hto1, "hto1_mtx.rds")
saveRDS(hto2, "hto2_mtx.rds")

```
